guard: an older cotal refuses a newer seed store without writing, names only a proven sufficient executable, and keeps the generic fallback otherwise
why: SIX MUTATIONS, ONE FOR EACH INDEPENDENT PROMISE. Extending the downgrade predicate with the
deterministic runtime-false `process.pid < 0` keeps TypeScript's store-generation narrowing while
disabling the refusal at runtime. Dropping the verified executable from the refusal removes
sufficient-path hinting while leaving the refusal intact. Making the
sufficiency predicate accept every verified executable admits a candidate below the store generation.
Removing the ephemeral-npx PATH guard admits a transient cache shim while the same executable
at a durable path remains verified. That mutation runs smoke:install, whose single discriminating
cell covers both halves and prints its completion line on green and red runs.
Each mutation is compile-clean and names the exact assertion for the promise it breaks.
Every anchor is code-only and unique. The refusal mutation keeps both semver predicates intact,
so it remains compile-clean and changes only whether the guarded refusal is reachable.
Each seed-source mutation rebuilds @cotal-ai/cli and runs the relevant real-binary downgrade case,
then rebuilds after restoration. The full seed suite runs separately. Restoring without rebuilding leaves dist
compiled from the mutant even though git reports a clean tree.
WHAT THIS DOES NOT PROVE, stated because the fix has a real limit. The guard ships in this
version and later. A binary RELEASED BEFORE it does not carry it and never will, so an old
cotal already on a machine can still downgrade a store it meets. That is why the smoke stamps
the store at 99.0.0 instead of running an actually-old build: 99.0.0 is newer than any binary
that will ever run the suite, which tests the comparison from the side the guard can defend.
Pointing a real v0.16.0 at a newer store reproduces the DEFECT, which is how it was found, and
proves nothing about the FIX.

mutations.name: force and reset again bypass backward-generation protection
mutations.find:
const downgrade = seedDowngradeRefusal(generation);
  if (downgrade) throw downgrade;
mutations.replace:
const downgrade = seedDowngradeRefusal(generation);
  if (downgrade && mode !== "reset" && mode !== "force") throw downgrade;
mutations.expectRed: ✗ FAIL: downgrade: --force cannot replace a newer shared generation
mutations.cell: ✗ FAIL: downgrade: --force cannot replace a newer shared generation
